title: devalue: devalue: Custom ArrayBuffer revivers can bypass typed-array allocation validation
provenance: Labels come from the maintainers' fix commit, not from a model: the lines it changed or removed in its parent commit (advisory GHSA-r9w8-h9r3-54w4). Whether the patch really addresses the advisory is recorded in history.label_review.
contamination: Advisory published 2026-10-01 and fix committed 2026-09-18, both on or after 2026-03-10, after the 2026-03-03 release of gemini-3.1-flash-lite (knowledge cutoff January 2025): that model cannot have trained on this fix. A model with a later cutoff might have. The code may still resemble earlier public fixes of similar bugs in the same project.

bugs.title: devalue: Custom ArrayBuffer revivers can bypass typed-array allocation validation
bugs.notes: The fix only adds code, so the label is the line just before the insertion; a correct finding may point at the unprotected code a few lines on, or elsewhere in the same function. Judge a finding against the advisory text in `history`, not only against the lines.

history.description: Under very specific circumstances, `parse` could create massive ArrayBuffers with very small input. This required a malformed `ArrayBuffer` custom reviver.
history.label_review: Claude read the fix patch against the advisory text on 2026-10-24 and found they match (one reader, not independently reviewed). Weak: the advisory is two sentences and the fix only adds validation before a typed-array constructor.
